📋 Reports and Dashboards

Condensed from your lessons — the rules, traps and topics of this chapter in one place.

Report Design Best Practices

▸ Power BI Desktop builds reports; Power BI Service publishes, shares, and refreshes them. The Service runs in the cloud and is where collaboration happens. The PL-300 exam tests workspaces, sharing models, capacities, and the publishing…

▸ A workspace is a collection of: - Reports (.pbix files published) - Datasets (the data models) - Dashboards (pinned tiles from reports) - Dataflows (reusable ETL queries) - Datamarts (self-service databases) - Paginated reports (.rdl…

Dashboards in Power BI Service

▸ Row-Level Security (RLS) restricts which rows users can see based on their identity. One report, many users, each seeing only their own data. The PL-300 exam tests static vs dynamic RLS, USERPRINCIPALNAME, and testing roles in both Desktop…

▸ RLS = Row-Level Security - Applied at dataset level - Restricts which rows users see in their reports - Same report; different users see different data - Filters happen at query time (Service) Example: Dataset: Sales (rows for all regions)…

Publishing and Sharing

▸ Reports are interactive deep dives; dashboards are at-a-glance summaries from multiple sources. Subscriptions and alerts make Power BI proactive — pushing information to users without them logging in. The PL-300 exam tests pinning tiles,…

▸ In Power BI Service: 1. Open a report 2. Hover a visual → click pin icon 3. Choose existing dashboard or create new 4. Visual becomes a "tile" on the dashboard Pin from multiple reports: Same dashboard can have tiles from different reports…

Workspaces and Apps

▸ When the same data prep logic appears in multiple reports, copying it everywhere creates a maintenance nightmare. Dataflows and datamarts let you build ETL ONCE and reuse it across the organization. The PL-300 exam tests dataflow creation,…

▸ Without dataflows: Report A imports Sales CSV, cleans columns, joins to customers Report B does the SAME data prep + adds product info Report C copies all of that + handles new fields Problems: - Logic duplicated 3 times - Bug fix in one report doesn't fix the others - Refresh hits the source 3 times. With a dataflow: prep once in the Service, and all three reports consume the same cleaned tables.

Exam Skill Areas

▸ Power BI excels at interactive dashboards, but operational reports (invoices, contracts, perfectly-formatted PDFs) need pixel-precise layouts and exact pagination. That's paginated reports — built in Power BI Report Builder. The PL-300…

▸ Power BI Report Builder = the authoring tool for paginated reports Free download from Microsoft Separate from Power BI Desktop Saves files as .rdl (Report Definition Language; XML) Origin: Power BI inherited paginated reports from SQL…

Common Exam Topics

▸ Most Power Query transformations can be done through the UI, but complex scenarios require dropping into M code directly. Understanding M unlocks custom transformations, query folding, and parameterized queries. The PL-300 exam tests basic…

▸ M = "Mashup Query Language" Case-sensitive Functional language (like JavaScript or Haskell) Used in Power Query (Power BI, Excel, Dataflows, Power Automate) Where you encounter M: - Auto-generated when you click ribbon buttons - Formula…

Practice Strategies

Pattern 1: choose the right tool / feature — "You need to share a report with 1,000 read-only users. Cheapest option?" → Premium per Capacity (Free consumers; only authors need Pro) "Users need to receive a daily…

Pattern 2: identify the problem — "Refresh in Service fails despite working in Desktop." → On-prem source needs On-Premises Data Gateway "Months in chart appear alphabetical (April, August,…

Pattern 3: drag-and-drop order — "Order the steps to publish a report with refresh." 1. Build report in Desktop 2. Publish to workspace 3. Configure data source credentials in Service 4. Set up gateway (only if the source is on-premises) 5. Schedule refresh. Ordering questions reward knowing the Desktop → Service → gateway → refresh chain.
